title: Interactive tool-call schema minimization and error mapper
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Provide a compact, implementation-friendly JSON schema format for tool/function call parameters that minimizes payload size for streaming scenarios, preserves human-readable diagnostics, and maps runtime validation failures to stable error classes for application-level handling. This ticket defines the schema layout (shorthand + full form), canonical validation rules, and an "error mapper" specification for converting runtime exceptions into deterministic error codes and developer-facing messages.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec document describing shorthand and canonical schema representations with examples for optional/required fields, arrays, nested objects, enums, and union types. 2) Validation behavior table mapping input errors (missing, type-mismatch, pattern, enum, extra-field) to stable error codes and suggested consumer messages. 3) Reference implementation (JS + Go) of the validator and error mapper with unit tests covering edge cases including streaming partial payloads. 4) E2E integration test in the runtime that demonstrates graceful fallback to a compatible model variant when validation returns a non-retryable error code. 5) Console telemetry hooks for tracking validation error classes by route and model.
design_notes:
- We will support two parallel representations: (A) compact shorthand optimized for low-bandwidth clients where common fields are positional or abbreviated, and (B) canonical expanded JSON for tooling and diagnostics. The runtime will normalize shorthand into canonical form before validation.
- Avoid schema-language proliferation: use a small set of type descriptors (string, number, boolean, object, array, enum, union) plus optional format/pattern/meta tags. Keep schema depth limited to 6 to avoid complexity in streaming scenarios.
- Validation must be deterministic and pure (no network calls). Side effects (e.g., KMS lookups) must be rejected with a separate error class.
- Error mapper will emit three axes: code (stable machine-readable), severity (info/warn/error), and user_message (short human text). Include an optional diagnostic hint with a small example of the offending fragment (up to 256 bytes) to preserve privacy.
- Backwards compatibility: introduce an opt-in header (X-RW-Schema-Version) to allow staged rollout. Default runtime still accepts legacy calls and applies best-effort coercions when safe (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers if schema allows). Coercions are logged and surfaced as a warning-class validation event.
tradeoffs:
- Compact shorthand reduces bytes but complicates authoring and increases normalization logic in the runtime. We accept this for streaming clients where network cost and latency matter.
- Coercion improves developer experience but can mask client bugs; we will make coercions opt-in per-route and warn by default.
- Providing diagnostic snippets helps debugging but has privacy implications; we cap snippets to 256 bytes and redact control characters.
- Keeping schema language minimal avoids expressivity for complex constraints (e.g., cross-field invariants). Those will be handled in downstream evals or business logic layers.
test_plan:
Unit tests for validator + error mapper across both representations. Fuzz tests to validate deterministic error mapping for malformed inputs. Integration tests: stream partial payloads split across frames to verify normalization is resilient to chunking. Load test to ensure validation adds <=3% P50 latency at 95th percentile in typical production config. Telemetry tests to verify events include schema version and error code.
- Test cases include: missing required, extra unknown field, type mismatch with/without coercion, enum mismatch, pattern failure, nested array length violations, and union resolution ambiguity.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge spec and reference impl behind feature flag. 2) Deploy validator to canary runtime with X-RW-Schema-Version opt-in header for internal customers. 3) Collect telemetry for 1 week, iterate on coercion rules and user_message wording. 4) Enable for broader customers with a 2-week slow rollout, defaulting to permissive coercions but emitting warnings. 5) Make stricter mode available via route config and document migration steps.
- Backout: feature flag off; runtime continues to support legacy validation behavior.
